stem: Which physical property quantifies a body's resistance to being set into or brought out of rotational motion? (a) Mass (b) Moment of inertia (c) Linear momentum (d) Torque —
Calculate the moment of inertia of a 4 kg solid sphere of radius 0.20 m about its diameter. (a) 0.032 kg m² (b) 0.064 kg m² (c) 0.080 kg m² (d) 0.160 kg m² —
A 2 kg solid sphere (R = 0.10 m) rotates about an axis 0.30 m from its centre. Find I about this axis. (a) 0.020 kg m² (b) 0.094 kg m² (c) 0.188 kg m² (d) 0.300 kg m² —

From a circular disc of radius R and mass 9 M, a small disc of radius R/3 is removed from the disc as shown in the figure (the hole touches the rim, so its centre lies at 2R/3 from the centre C). Find the moment of inertia of the remaining disc about an axis perpendicular to the plane of the disc and passing through the point 'O'. — 📝 PYQ: JEE Main 2018 Solution ↗

Find the moment of inertia of the system about the given axis: a rod of mass m and length 3R is hinged at the axis of rotation (perpendicular to the rod) and a uniform solid sphere of mass 10 m and radius R is fixed at its far end, the sphere touching the rod's end so that the sphere's centre is 4R from the axis. —

A metallic ring of mass 1 kg has moment of inertia 1 kg m² when rotating about one of its diameters. It is molten and re-molded into a thin uniform disc of the same radius. How much will its moment of inertia be, when rotated about its own axis. — (Level: Board)

A big dumb-bell is prepared by using a uniform rod of mass 60 g and length 20 cm. Two identical solid spheres of mass 50 g and radius 10 cm each are at the two ends of the rod. Calculate moment of inertia of the dumb-bell when rotated about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to the length. — (Level: Board)
The M.O.I. of ring of mass 0.5 kg and radius 50 cm about diameter of ring is x × 10 −2 kg-m², then find x . —
Find the M.O.I. of a uniform square plate of mass 2 kg and side 0.5 cm about an axis passing through centre and perpendicular to the plane of plate. (in kg-m²) —
Which of the following has the smallest moment of inertia about the central axis if all have equal masses and radii? (a) Ring (b) Disc (c) Spherical shell (d) Sphere —

The moment of inertia of a thin uniform circular disc about one of the diameters is I. Its moment of inertia about an axis perpendicular to the plane of the disc and passing through its centre is: (a) (√2)I (b) 2I (c) I/2 (d) 1/√2 —
The moment of inertia of a circular ring of radius r and mass M about diameter is: (a) 2/5 Mr² (b) Mr²/4 (c) Mr²/2 (d) Mr²/12 — 📝 PYQ: AIEEE 2002 Solution ↗
The M.O.I. of ring of mass 0.5 kg and radius 50 cm about an axis tangent to ring is x × 10 −2 kg-m², then find x . —
Find the M.O.I. of ring of mass 0.5 kg and radius 50 cm about an axis passing through a point on circumference and perpendicular to plane of ring. (in kg-m²) —
Find M.O.I. of disc of mass 1 kg and radius 25 cm about an axis passing through a point at the edge and perpendicular to plane of disc is x × 10 −2 kg-m², find x . —
Find the M.O.I. of a solid sphere of mass 5 kg and radius 25 cm about an axis tangent to sphere. (in kg-m²) —
Find the M.O.I. of a uniform hollow sphere of mass 2 kg and radius 25 cm about an axis tangent to sphere. (in kg-m²) —
A solid sphere of mass 5 kg and radius 0.2 m is rotating about its diameter. Find its moment of inertia. (a) 0.08 kg m² (b) 0.16 kg m² (c) 0.04 kg m² (d) 0.32 kg m² —
Find the M.O.I. of a uniform square plate of mass 2 kg and side 0.5 m about an axis co-inciding with the sides of plate. (in kg-m²) —
Find the moment of inertia of a 5 kg plate 0.30 m × 0.40 m about an axis perpendicular to the plane and 0.25 m away from its centre. (a) 0.30 kg m² (b) 0.46 kg m² (c) 0.59 kg m² (d) 0.75 kg m² —

Consider a uniform square plate of side ‘a’ and mass ‘m’. Moment of inertia of this plate about an axis perpendicular to its plane and passing through one of its corners is: (a) 5/6 ma² (b) ma²/12 (c) 7ma²/12 (d) (2/3)ma² — 📝 PYQ: AIEEE 2008 Solution ↗
The M.O.I. of a rod of mass of 0.25 kg and length 1 m about an axis perpendicular to the rod and at a distance 30 cm from one end is x × 10 −2 kg-m², find x . —

key: c If the axes are parallel, I A < I B
stem: Let I A and I B be moments of inertia of a body about two axes A and B respectively. The axis A passes through the centre of mass of the body but B does not. (a) I A < I B (b) If I A < I B , the axes are parallel (c) If the axes are parallel, I A < I B (d) If the axes are not parallel, I A ≥ I B —
Find the radius of gyration of a circular ring of radius r about a line perpendicular to the plane of the ring and passing through one of its particles. —
The radius of gyration of a uniform disc about a line perpendicular to the disc equals its radius. Find the distance of the line from the centre. —

The ratio of the radii of gyration of a circular disc about a tangential axis in the plane of the disc and of a circular ring of the same radius about a tangential axis in the plane of the ring is: (a) 2 : 1 (b) √5 : √6 (c) 2 : 3 (d) 1 : √2 —

Two rings of the same radius r and mass m are placed such that their centres are at a common point and their planes are perpendicular to each other. The moment of inertia of the system about an axis passing through the centre and perpendicular to the plane of one of the ring is: (a) (1/2) mr² (b) mr² (c) (3/2) mr² (d) 2 mr² —

A uniform square plate of side 2 m and mass 6 kg lies in a horizontal plane. An axis passes through the centre of the plate and lies in its plane, making an angle 30° with one of its sides. Find the moment of inertia of the plate about this axis. (a) 2 kg/m² (b) 3 kg/m² (c) 4 kg/m² (d) 5 kg/m² —

Figure shows a uniform rectangular sheet with BC = 2AB. Moment of inertia of the sheet is minimum about: (a) AC (b) PQ (c) RS (d) AD. [In the figure D and C are the top corners, A and B the bottom corners; PQ is the line joining the midpoints of DC and AB, and RS the line joining the midpoints of AD and BC.] —
For the given uniform square lamina ABCD, whose centre is O, [EF joins the midpoints of AB and DC, and AC is a diagonal] (a) I AC = √2 I EF (b) √2 I AC = I EF (c) I AD = 3 I EF (d) I AC = I EF —
Find the moment of inertia of a pair of spheres, each having a mass m and radius r, kept in contact about the tangent passing through the point of contact. —

The moment of inertia of a thin square plate ABCD of uniform thickness about an axis passing through the centre O and perpendicular to the plate is: (i) I 1 + I 2 (ii) I 3 + I 4 (iii) I 1 + I 3 (iv) I 1 + I 2 + I 3 + I 4 , where I 1 , I 2 , I 3 and I 4 are respectively the moment of inertia about axes 1, 2, 3 and 4 which are in the plane of the plate [1 and 2 are the two diagonals, 3 and 4 the central lines parallel to the sides]. (a) (i, ii) (b) (ii, iii) (c) (i, iv) (d) (i, ii, iii) —
Find the moment of inertia of a uniform square plate of mass m and edge a about one of its diagonals. —

If the moment of inertia of a disc about an axis tangentially and parallel to its surface be I, then the moment of inertia about the axis tangential but perpendicular to the surface will be (a) 6/5 I (b) ¾I (c) 3/2 I (d) 5/4 I —

Let I be the moment of inertia of a uniform square plate about an axis AB that passes through its centre and is parallel to two of its sides. CD is a line in the plane of the plate that passes through the centre of the plate and makes an angle θ with AB. The moment of inertia of the plate about the axis CD is then equal to (a) I (b) I sin²θ (c) I cos²θ (d) I cos²(θ/2) —

Three uniform rods, each of mass ‘M’ and length ‘L’ form the sides of an equilateral triangle. Moment of inertia of this system about an axis passing through a corner and perpendicular to the plane of triangle is: (a) (5/2)ML² (b) (3/2)ML² (c) (7/2)ML² (d) ML² —

A solid sphere of mass M, radius R and having moment of inertia about an axis passing through the centre of mass as I, is recast into a disc of thickness t, whose moment of inertia about an axis passing through its edge and perpendicular to its plane remains I. Then, radius of the disc will be: (a) 2R/√15 (b) R√(2/15) (c) 4R/√15 (d) R/4 — 📝 PYQ: IIT-JEE 2006 Solution ↗
A thin uniform wire of length ℓ and mass ‘m’ is bent in the form of a semi-circle. Calculate its moment of inertia about an axis (Y′OY) passing through the free ends. —

A uniform rod of mass m is bent into a semicircle of radius R. The moment of inertia of the rod about an axis passing through P and perpendicular to plane of semicircular ring is: (a) mR² (b) 2mR² (c) (2/3)mR² (d) (5/π)mR² [P is one end of the bounding diameter, O the centre] —

Two identical rings each of mass m with their planes mutually perpendicular, radius R are welded at their point of contact O. If the system is free to rotate about an axis passing through the point P perpendicular to the plane of the paper, the moment of inertia of the system about this axis is equal to (a) 6.5 mR² (b) 12 mR² (c) 6 mR² (d) 11.5 mR² [the lower ring lies in the plane of the paper with centre O; the upper ring stands perpendicular to the paper, touching it at the top of the lower ring, and P is the highest point of the upper ring, 3R above O] —

A uniform solid sphere of radius R has a cavity of radius R/2 as shown. Mass of this system is M. Find moment of inertia of this sphere about an axis passing through centre of sphere. (a) (57/140)MR² (b) (16/35)MR² (c) MR²/28 (d) MR²/20 [the spherical cavity touches the outer surface internally, its centre lying at R/2 from the sphere's centre; the axis passes through the sphere's centre, perpendicular to the line of centres] —

Find the moment of inertia of a hemisphere of mass M (shown in the figure) about an axis AA′ passing through its centre of mass. [AA′ is perpendicular to the hemisphere’s symmetry axis, i.e. parallel to the flat face’s diameter.] —
The radius of gyration of a solid hemisphere of mass M and radius R about an axis parallel to the diameter at a distance 3R/4 from this plane is given by (a) 3R/√10 (b) 5R/4 (c) 5R/8 (d) √(2/5) R —

A uniform disc of radius R lies in the XY-plane with its center at origin. Its moment of inertia about Z-axis is equal to its moment of inertia about line y = x + c. The value of c can be (a) −R/2 (b) R/√2 (c) R/4 (d) None —

Two rings of the same radius and mass are placed, such that their centres are at a common point and their planes are perpendicular to each other. The moment of inertia of the system about an axis passing through the centre and perpendicular to the plane of one of the rings is (mass of the ring = m, radius = r) (a) ½mr² (b) mr² (c) (3/2)mr² (d) 2mr² —

Three rings each of mass m and radius r are placed in a plane touching each other as shown. The radius of gyration of the system about the axis as shown in the figure is (a) √(7/6) r (b) √(5/3) r (c) √(5/6) r (d) √(7/2) r [the axis is the vertical line in the plane of the rings, through the centre of the upper ring and through the contact point of the two lower rings] —

A square plate of mass M and edge L is shown in figure. The moment of inertia of the plate about the axis in the plane of plate passing through one of its vertex making an angle 15° from horizontal is (a) ML²/12 (b) 11ML²/24 (c) 7ML²/12 (d) None of these —
The moment of inertia of a cube of mass m and side a about the diagonal of one of its face is (a) ma²/12 (b) ma²/6 (c) 5ma²/12 (d) 2ma²/3 —

A table tennis bat has a flat rectangular handle of mass m and length ℓ and a flat circular disc of radius r and mass m attached to the handle. The moment of inertia of the bat about an axis perpendicular to its plane and passing through its centre of mass is: (a) mℓ²/12 + mr²/2 (b) mℓ²/3 + 3mr²/2 (c) 2m(ℓ/2 + r)² (d) mℓ²/12 + mr²/2 + (m/8)(ℓ + 2r)² —

AB and CD are two identical rods each of length l and mass m joined to form a cross is fixed inside a ring of mass m and radius l /2. Moment of inertia of the system about a bisector of the angle between the rods (XY) is (a) 7m l ²/6 (b) 13m l ²/12 (c) m l ²/12 (d) 5m l ²/24 —

A disc of radius R/2 is cut from a uniform disc of radius R as shown in the figure. The mass of the disc (with cavity) is M. The moment of inertia of this disc about an axis XX′ which passes through the centre O of the disc and is in the plane of the disc will be (a) 7MR²/12 (b) 13MR²/24 (c) 13MR²/48 (d) 11MR²/36 [the hole is centred at R/2 from O and touches the rim; XX′ is drawn through O at 45° to the line of centres] —

A uniform rod of mass 2M is bent into four adjacent semi-circles each of radius r, all lying in the same plane. The moment of inertia of the bent rod about an axis through one end A and perpendicular to plane of rod is (a) 22Mr² (b) 88Mr² (c) 44Mr² (d) 66Mr² —
